summary: Implemented server-driven pagination in renderProjectList (app.js):
- Updated getProjects() API method to accept params object and build query string
- Replaced client-side renderProjectList with new server-driven version:
• buildTable(): renders rows without local sorting (server already sorted)
• buildPagination(): generates prev/page#/next buttons with ellipsis logic, page-size selector (25/50/100), and 'Showing X-Y of Z projects' info text
• buildStatusOptions(): builds status filter options with per-status counts from envelope.status_counts
• render(envelope): accepts ProjectListEnvelope; all event handlers reattached per render
• load(): calls API.getProjects with all pagination params and passes envelope to render()
• State: currentPage, pageLimit, currentStatus, currentSort, currentDir persisted in localStorage
• Search: 300ms debounce, resets page to 1
• 10-second poll refreshes current page
- Removed orphaned old function body (269 lines) left after initial partial replacement

- Added pagination CSS to styles.css: .pagination-row, .pagination, .pagination-btn, .pagination-btn.active, .pagination-btn:disabled, .pagination-ellipsis, .pagination-info, .page-size-row, .page-size-selector with dark mode variants
All 1200 tests pass

comments.note: app.js: The renderProjectList function is now ~350 lines. While necessary for full pagination/filter/sort functionality in vanilla JS, extracting buildTable, buildPagination, and buildStatusOptions as module-level helpers would improve testability. Not done here as it would require restructuring the entire SPA script.

app.js: getProjects() builds the query string with manual string concatenation using encodeURIComponent. A small helper function (buildQueryString) would make this more maintainable if more API methods need query parameters in the future.

styles.css: Pagination dark mode overrides use [data-theme='dark'] attribute selectors rather than @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark). This is consistent with the rest of styles.css — no change needed.

summary: QA PASS for WP-008 Frontend Pagination.
Test suite: 1200/1200 pass. TypeScript: clean compile (exit 0).
All 11 acceptance criteria verified against implementation:
1. buildPagination() generates prev/page-buttons/next correctly; start/end math handles edge cases (total=0, partial last page).
2. Page size selector (25/50/100) initialised from localStorage with NaN/invalid guard; onChange persists to localStorage, resets page=1.
3. Pagination btn click handler guards disabled state, updates currentPage (prev: max(1,n-1), next: min(lastTotalPages,n+1)), calls load().

4. thSort adds sort-asc/sort-desc class on active column; handleSortAction toggles dir on same key, sets dir by column type for new key, resets page=1, persists to localStorage. Keyboard (Enter/Space) also handled.
5. Status filter change: resets page=1, persists to localStorage, calls load().
6. Search input: 300ms debounce with clearTimeout guard, resets page=1 inside timeout callback.
7. buildStatusOptions: appends ' (N)' count for concrete statuses (not ACTIVE/ALL) from server status_counts.
8. 'Showing X–Y of Z' text: correct for zero total, partial last page, and full pages.
9. Auto-poll: Router._setPolling(load, 10000) — load() uses live currentPage/pageLimit/currentStatus/currentSearch/currentSort/currentDir closures.
10. Prev disabled when page===1; Next disabled when page===total_pages; click handler has if(this.disabled)return guard.

11. CSS: .pagination-btn, .active, :disabled (opacity 0.4, cursor not-allowed), :hover:not(:disabled):not(.active), .pagination-ellipsis, .page-size-row/.page-size-selector, dark mode [data-theme='dark'] variants — all present in styles.css.

metrics.test_coverage: 1200/1200 unit+integration tests pass; TypeScript compiles clean

comments.note: app.js renderProjectList: The manual 'Refresh' button resets currentPage=1 before calling load(), which is slightly inconsistent with the 10-second auto-poll (which stays on current page). This is a minor UX decision, not a defect — no AC covers manual refresh page behavior.

app.js buildPagination: When total_pages===1 the pagination button row is suppressed entirely (intentional — no need for nav buttons on a single page). The 'Showing X–Y of Z' info and page-size selector still render. AC10 (prev disabled on page 1 / next disabled on last page) is satisfied because neither button is shown, not because they are shown-but-disabled. Acceptable UX pattern.

app.js: page-navigation 'next' uses lastTotalPages closure variable (set at last render). If the total_pages shrinks between renders (e.g. bulk deletions), the next button could momentarily show as enabled. In practice the 10-second auto-poll self-corrects; no AC impact.

summary: Code review PASS for WP-008 Frontend Pagination (app.js + styles.css).

Reviewed: getProjects() API client, renderProjectList closure, buildTable/buildPagination/buildStatusOptions helpers, render/load pattern, event listener wiring, localStorage persistence, auto-poll integration, and all CSS pagination rules.

Architecture is sound: full state closure (currentPage, pageLimit, currentStatus, currentSearch, currentSort, currentDir) with localStorage-backed persistence where appropriate. NaN guard on pageLimit initialization is correct. Debounce pattern captures val at event time — no stale-read risk.

buildPagination: zero-total edge case handled (start=0 guard), window-of-pages uses Object.keys().sort() to prevent key-ordering ambiguity — correct. disabled attribute on prev/next is set in HTML, and click handler has if(this.disabled)return guard — doubly safe.
No listener leaks: app.innerHTML replacement nukes the old DOM on every render; each new thead/btn gets exactly one fresh listener.
All 11 distinct acceptance criteria confirmed met by implementation. 1200/1200 tests pass per QA. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: app.js getProjects(): manual query-string builder with encodeURIComponent is functional but verbose. A small buildQueryString(params) helper would improve maintainability if additional API methods gain query parameters. Non-blocking — already flagged by Developer.

app.js renderProjectList(): handleSortAction is redeclared inside render() on every call. This is harmless (old DOM is replaced before the new listener attaches), but extracting it as a stable function reference would make the code slightly easier to reason about. Not a defect.

app.js buildPagination(): When total_pages === 1, pagination nav buttons are suppressed entirely rather than showing disabled prev/next. This is a valid and common UX pattern (no need for nav with one page). AC-10 (prev disabled on page 1 / next disabled on last page) is satisfied by omission. QA already flagged this edge case — confirming it is acceptable.

app.js: Manual Refresh button resets currentPage = 1 before load(), while auto-poll stays on current page. Minor UX inconsistency — arguably a user expectation that manual refresh goes to page 1. No AC coverage. Not a defect, but worth noting for a future UX decision.

summary: Updated mcp-server/README.md GUI Features section to reflect WP-008 server-driven pagination:

- Replaced 'Sortable columns' (client-side) bullet with 'Server-driven sort' accurately describing server-side sort with reset-to-page-1 behaviour; localStorage keys (mcp-sort-key / mcp-sort-dir) and defaults unchanged.

- Added new 'Pagination' bullet documenting Previous/page-number/Next controls, page-size selector (25/50/100) persisted via mcp-page-limit, 'Showing X-Y of Z projects' summary, and clarifying that the 10-second auto-refresh polls the current page (not always page 1).

- Replaced 'Fulltext search' (instant client-side filter) bullet with 'Search & filter' describing 300 ms debounced server-side search, per-status counts in the status dropdown (e.g. Ready (3)), and mcp-status-filter localStorage persistence defaulting to ACTIVE.

comments.note: README.md: The three new feature bullets accurately reflect the implementation. The localStorage key list in the README now covers all five persisted keys: mcp-theme, mcp-sort-key, mcp-sort-dir, mcp-page-limit, mcp-status-filter — no additional documentation gaps found.
